# MenuList System Data Flow Audit - 2026-06-20

## Scope

System-level MenuList audit focused on live data flow, cache consistency, owner/mobile parity, public customer output, API guardrails, AI accounting presentation, and background Firebase writers.

Excluded from MenuList findings:

- Answerlattice, CampaignCue, GrowthOS, and Canonica product surfaces unless shared MenuList infrastructure was affected.
- Vercel deployment. App-side route fixes were validated locally but not deployed.

Firebase Functions logic changed in this pass, so MenuList Functions deployment is required after validation. Deployment status is tracked at the end of this document.

## Fix Ledger

### June 30 follow-up: CampaignCue API security-log boundary

Status: Fixed.

The CampaignCue shared API guard already enforced the CampaignCue feature flag, authenticated sessions, tenant/store scope checks, hashed limiter key segments, configured route limits, bounded JSON body parsing, generic malformed-JSON responses, and product-scoped API boundaries. Its tenant-violation, rate-limit, malformed-JSON, and Design Cue validation security events still spread raw `buildSecurityContext(session, request)` output or logged raw route/feature/validation fields.

`src/lib/campaigncue/apiGuards.ts` now builds guard security payloads through `getCampaignCueSecurityLogContext()`, backed by `getBoundedSecurityRouteContext()` plus bounded endpoint/method metadata. Tenant, store, user, feature, and validation metadata remain presence/length fields. `src/app/api/campaigncue/design-cue/turns/route.ts` now uses the same bounded context for validation failures. `scripts/verification/verify-campaigncue-runtime.js` now guards the bounded context helper, endpoint/method metadata, raw-context bans, raw endpoint bans, raw feature bans, and raw Design Cue validation-error bans.

Validation: `npm run verify:campaigncue`, `npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false --pretty false`, scoped `git diff --check`, and raw-pattern scans passed in this session.

Impact: valid CampaignCue feature gating, tenant/store scope checks, rate limits, JSON body admission, Design Cue model-assist fail-closed behavior, response statuses, CampaignCue Firestore reads/writes, rules/indexes, Cloud Functions, Firebase deploy requirement, owner workspace behavior, and Vercel deploy execution remain unchanged. This is CampaignCue security-log metadata hardening only.

The endpoint now uses shared rate limiting before Firestore lookup at `src/app/api/screen/seen/route.ts:73`, with the shared `SCREEN_SEEN_SIGNAL` config at `src/lib/rateLimit/configs.ts:232`. It also applies a stricter token/store key limit before the daily Firestore write.

Status: Fixed, including the adjacent issue found during the restart audit.

The public icon, screenshot, and splash image routes now validate store ID shape and apply the shared `PUBLIC_DYNAMIC_ASSET` limiter before reading `stores/{storeId}`:

- Icons: `src/app/api/app-icons/[storeId]/[size]/route.tsx:35`
- Screenshots: `src/app/api/app-screenshots/[storeId]/[formFactor]/route.tsx:152`
- Splash images: `src/app/api/app-splash/[storeId]/[size]/route.tsx:32`

June 28 follow-up: icon, splash, and screenshot generation failures now use stable runtime failure codes with store-id presence/length metadata plus size/dimension/form-factor values and source error name/code/status only. `npm run verify:customer-app-pwa` guards the bounded icon, splash, and screenshot route contracts.

### 15. Public create-menu upload body cap ran after multipart parsing

Status: Fixed during the June 26 restart audit.

`POST /api/public/create-menu` now rejects requests over the 10MB image limit plus multipart overhead by `content-length` and reads multipart uploads through the shared bounded form-data helper before file access. The application/json link-import path uses an 8KB bounded body reader before link validation. The extraction pipeline verifier now checks both source orderings.

### 28. All API route direct body-reader coverage was only a manual sweep

Status: Verifier invariant added during the June 27 continuation audit.

`npm run verify:menulist-api-tenant-safety` now recursively scans every `src/app/api/**/route.ts(x)` file and fails if any route uses direct `request`/`req` body readers: `json()`, `text()`, `arrayBuffer()`, `blob()`, or `formData()`, including whitespace variants. ### 153. KB Quality output storage and cost contract was inconsistent with implementation

Status: Fixed during the June 28 continuation audit.

The KB Quality review found a contract mismatch that needed a dedicated storage/cost change. The feature docs described one store-level output document at `insights/{tId}/stores/{sId}/ai/kbQuality`, one write per store, and one Gemini call per store. The implementation analyzed articles one by one, attempted to write each article result through `db.collection("insights/{tId}/stores/{sId}/ai/kbQuality").doc(articleId)`, and therefore mixed a per-article output model with the documented per-store AI insight document. That storage/cost contract affected Firestore shape, Gemini cost accounting, future readers, and verifier expectations.

`functions/src/analytics/kbQuality.ts` now implements the documented store-level contract. It gathers existing article/query signals, caps Gemini input to the top 10 signal-bearing articles with 5 query examples per signal type, calls `analyzeKBStoreQuality()` once per store, and writes one `insights/{tId}/stores/{sId}/ai/kbQuality` document through the same `DB_COLLECTIONS.INSIGHTS -> stores -> ai -> kbQuality` pattern as Feedback Intelligence and Weekly Narrative. `functions/src/services/gemini/kbQuality.ts` now has a store-level prompt/parser/fallback path with stable `GEMINI_KB_QUALITY_STORE_FAILED` diagnostics while preserving the old article helper for non-scheduler callers. `npm run verify:auth-security-failure-matrix` now guards the store-level call, one-doc output path, `v1-store` prompt marker, and old invalid per-article collection-path patterns.

It reduces Gemini calls from up to one per signal-bearing article to one bounded call per store and keeps Firestore writes at one per analyzed store. Existing article reads, query-signal reads, scheduler task wiring, telemetry writes, and no-data skip behavior remain unchanged. It now uses bounded `functions.logger` metadata, disables local file writes in production, and `npm run verify:auth-security-failure-matrix` covers the helper directly.
- Functions realtime tracking review found the unused realtime helper still direct-console logged raw session IDs, store context, and provider/runtime failures. It now uses bounded analytics diagnostics and stable local failure codes, and `npm run verify:auth-security-failure-matrix` covers the helper directly.
- POS sync route review found webhook validation text, HTTP failure text, timeout labels, and connection fallback text could be persisted into `posSync.lastError` or returned through POS sync API responses, with legacy mobile `lastError` display preserving old raw values. The POS test/delivery routes and mobile POS screen now expose fixed owner-safe connection text only, and `npm run verify:menulist-api-tenant-safety` covers the route and mobile display contract directly.
- Public create-menu draft review found failed draft polling returned stored `extractionError` directly and the shared extraction worker persisted raw `error.message` into job failures. The route now returns fixed public retry copy for failed drafts, the worker stores `Menu extraction failed`, and `npm run verify:menu-extraction-pipeline` covers the route/worker raw-message bans directly.
- Functions ops trigger review found publish verification, force republish, budget alert, and stores-summary backfill failure paths still returned or logged raw exception text and raw operational identifiers. `functions/src/triggers/operations.ts` now uses stable `OPERATIONS_*` codes, fixed callable copy, bounded metadata, and `npm run verify:menulist-api-tenant-safety` covers the trigger directly.

## Cost Impact

- Screen seen, PWA dynamic assets, CSP reports, and domain provider routes now have stronger rate/cost bounds.
- Scheduled special-menu and reconciliation cache invalidation add small bounded cache invalidation calls after existing writes.
- Claim-account cache invalidation adds no Firestore read/write; it refreshes existing Next.js public cache tags after existing store email writes.
- Screen seen cheap-fail hardening adds no Firestore read/write; it prevents oversized anonymous bodies and rate-limited IPs from reaching JSON parsing or Firestore lookup.
- Public create-menu body-size hardening adds no Firestore read/write; it blocks oversized upload requests before form parsing, buffering, Storage, draft, or job work.
- Razorpay webhook body-size/rate hardening adds no Firestore read/write; it blocks malformed, oversized, and rate-limited public webhook requests before signature validation, JSON parsing, idempotency claims, or billing mutations.
- Messaging preview approve/fix body-size hardening adds no Firestore read/write; it blocks oversized token-action bodies before JSON parsing and before publish/fix reads or writes.
- Menu extraction JSON body hardening adds no Firestore read/write; it blocks oversized owner upload/link/intake/claim control requests before parsing and before project/draft reads, source fetches, or extraction job writes.
- AI route body-size hardening adds no Firestore read/write; it blocks oversized provider-backed AI requests before parsing and before capacity, provider, or accounting work.
- Shared AI accounting diagnostic hardening adds no Firestore reads/writes, Storage operations, provider calls, route calls, credit debits, cache invalidations, rules, indexes, schema changes, tenant-shape changes, permission-model changes, public routes, durable event streams, or owner-facing settings. Existing operation-log best-effort behavior, paid-request credit-consumption failure behavior, and Answerlattice credit-consumption balance-detail merge behavior remain unchanged; only failure diagnostics are bounded.
- Billing/reseller mutation body-size and reseller write-throttle hardening adds no Firestore read/write for rejected requests; it blocks oversized, malformed, or rate-limited payment/reseller action bodies before provider calls, tenant/store reads, subscription writes, owner/reseller account creation, or entitlement sync.

## June 29 Follow-up: Transaction and Mobile Ops Payload Displays Bounded

The next owner/platform display sweep found three browser-side raw-payload gaps:

- `/api/ai-operations` returned full operation documents to platform transaction-history browsers, and desktop/mobile transaction detail panels rendered the full operation JSON.
- Desktop/mobile scheduler monitors bounded structured detail maps but still allowed historical `tasks[].error` text or mobile nested detail objects to render directly.
- The mobile custom-domain screen rendered Vercel verification config as raw JSON while the desktop domain settings tab already normalized it into DNS records.

Fixes:

- `src/app/api/ai-operations/route.ts` now uses `PLATFORM_VISIBLE_FIELDS` plus `sanitizePlatformOperation()` for platform transaction rows. Platform rows keep owner-visible transaction fields plus accounting audit fields such as model, token counts, charges, margin, project ID, file ID, and transaction ID, but no longer return raw provider response fields, generation config, token-usage internals, raw batch/provider payloads, or tenant/store/user IDs to transaction-history browsers.
- `src/components/templates/main-app/transactions/TransactionDetailsModal.tsx` and `src/components/mobile/screens/MobileTransactionsScreen.tsx` keep platform accounting rows but no longer render full transaction JSON.
- `src/components/templates/main-app/transactions/transaction-details/ImageProcessingDetailsView.tsx` no longer renders raw `clientResponse` JSON for B2B tenants; it uses the same extracted-row presentation as other tenant types. The dedicated B2B project JSON editor remains unchanged.
- `src/components/templates/main-app/platform/schedulerMonitor/index.tsx` and `src/components/mobile/screens/MobileSchedulerMonitorScreen.tsx` render task details and task error text as type/length/shape summaries.
- The former standalone custom-domain mobile screen was later removed; `MobileDomainSettingsScreen` remains the active mobile DNS setup surface.
- `scripts/verification/verify-ai-accounting-hardening.js` now guards the AI-operations platform allowlist and rejects full transaction JSON rendering.
- `scripts/verification/verify-menulist-api-tenant-safety.js` now guards bounded scheduler task details/errors and mobile custom-domain DNS display.

Validation:

```bash
npm run verify:ai-accounting
npm run verify:menulist-api-tenant-safety
npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false --pretty false
```

Result: all passed.

Cost/deploy boundary: this is MenuList app/API and UI hardening only. It adds no Firestore reads/writes/deletes, Storage operations, provider calls, cache invalidations, rules, indexes, schema changes, Cloud Function logic changes, owner-facing settings, or Firebase deploy requirement. Existing transaction pagination, owner-visible transaction fields, AI accounting writes, custom-domain add/check/remove behavior, scheduler reads, and manual recovery behavior are unchanged.

## June 29 Follow-up: Owner Notification Monitor Error Display Guard

After the owner-notification ops API had already been hardened to return compact error codes or stored-text presence/length summaries, the browser dashboard still rendered event and delivery `error` fields directly. That was safe for the current API response, but it left the UI without a second boundary if an older response shape or future route regression returned long stored provider/error text.

Fixes:

- `src/components/templates/main-app/platform/ownerNotificationMonitor/index.tsx` now routes event-list errors, selected-event errors, and delivery-attempt errors through `formatMonitorError()`.
- Compact local codes remain visible for recovery work.
- Existing stored-text summaries such as `Stored error present (N chars).`, `Subject present (N chars).`, and `Provider message id present (N chars).` remain visible.
- Any other long text is reduced to `Stored error present (N chars).` before rendering.
- `scripts/verification/verify-menulist-api-tenant-safety.js` now requires the display guard and rejects the old direct error render patterns.

Validation:

```bash
npm run verify:menulist-api-tenant-safety
npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false --pretty false
git diff --check
```

Cost/deploy boundary: this is MenuList platform UI defense-in-depth only. It adds no Firestore reads/writes/deletes, Storage operations, provider calls, cache invalidations, rules, indexes, schema changes, Cloud Function logic changes, owner-facing settings, Firebase deploy requirement, or Vercel deploy action in this session. Existing owner-notification event reads, delivery reads, recipient resolution, retry/manual-send/manual-handoff actions, and manual recovery flows are unchanged.

## June 29 Follow-up: Platform Notification WhatsApp Open Diagnostics

The browser-handoff sweep found both platform notification recovery dashboards already used safe `_blank` flags for manual WhatsApp Web messages, but blocked browser opens stayed silent. These handoffs are operator-only recovery paths for platform alerts and owner notification failures, so failed opens need bounded diagnostics without exposing recipient numbers or prefilled message bodies.

Fixes:

- `src/components/templates/main-app/platform/platformNotificationMonitor/index.tsx` now checks the returned WhatsApp Web window and logs `platform_notification_monitor_whatsapp_open_failed` when the browser blocks or rejects the handoff.
- `src/components/templates/main-app/platform/ownerNotificationMonitor/index.tsx` now checks the returned WhatsApp Web window and logs `owner_notification_monitor_whatsapp_open_failed` when the browser blocks or rejects the handoff.
- Diagnostics record selected event/filter context plus bounded destination, message-body, and WhatsApp URL presence-length metadata only.
- Raw recipient numbers, operator messages, WhatsApp URLs, provider messages, browser messages, and exception text are not logged directly.
- `scripts/verification/verify-menulist-api-tenant-safety.js` now guards both monitor WhatsApp open diagnostics, blocked-open checks, bounded context, and fixed failure copy.

Validation:

```bash
npm run verify:menulist-api-tenant-safety
npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false --pretty false

```

Cost/deploy boundary: this is MenuList platform-operator browser-handoff diagnostics and docs parity only. It adds no Firestore reads/writes/deletes, Storage operations, provider calls, cache invalidations, API routes, rules, indexes, schema changes, Cloud Function logic changes, owner-facing settings, Firebase deploy requirement, or Vercel deploy action. Existing platform notification reads, owner notification reads, retry, manual send, manual handoff recording, alert acknowledgement, and Email handoff behavior remain unchanged.

## June 29 Follow-up: Translation Provider Response Accounting Bounded

The AI-route raw-payload sweep found that `/api/translations` still set `geminiResponse: JSON.stringify(response)` in its route transaction object. The shared AI-operation logger already compacts provider responses, but pre-stringifying in the route made translation the outlier and could turn detailed-mode/local-development diagnostics into route-built provider-response string summaries instead of the standard response object usage/length summary.

Fixes:

- `src/app/api/translations/route.ts` now passes `geminiResponse: response` into `finalizeAiOperationAccounting()`.
- `scripts/verification/verify-ai-accounting-hardening.js` now rejects `geminiResponse: JSON.stringify(response)` in the translation route and requires the shared serializer path.

Validation:

```bash
npm run verify:ai-accounting
npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false --pretty false
git diff --check
```

Cost/deploy boundary: this is MenuList app-route accounting/logging hardening only. It adds no Firestore reads/writes/deletes, Storage operations, provider calls, cache invalidations, rules, indexes, schema changes, Cloud Function logic changes, owner-facing settings, Firebase deploy requirement, or Vercel deploy action in this session. Existing translation prompts, Gemini calls, retry/parsing behavior, normalized owner response, translation coverage accounting, AI accounting write shape, and credit consumption are unchanged.

## June 29 Follow-up: Scheduler Monitor Run Errors Bounded

After task details and task errors were bounded, the desktop scheduler monitor still had run-level stored error displays that printed `err.error` or `state.error` directly in failed settlement rows, the Last Run Errors panel, and expanded run-history rows. Those values are platform-only operational diagnostics, but they can contain historical provider or scheduler exception text and should use the same display guard as task errors.

Fixes:

- `src/components/templates/main-app/platform/schedulerMonitor/index.tsx` now routes failed settlement `state.error`, Last Run Errors labels/details, and run-history `errors[].error` rows through `formatStoredSchedulerError()`.
- `formatTaskError()` now delegates to the same formatter, keeping task/run error display behavior aligned.
- `scripts/verification/verify-menulist-api-tenant-safety.js` now requires the scheduler stored-error formatter and rejects the old direct run-level error render patterns.

## June 29 Follow-up: Mobile Domain Settings DNS Parity

The mobile DNS display sweep found that the active combined `MobileDomainSettingsScreen` kept a narrow local parser that only understood Vercel `verificationRecords`. That meant the live mobile Domain surface could show incomplete DNS guidance for Vercel response shapes that also used `configuredBy` or fallback CNAME values.

Fixes:

- `src/components/mobile/screens/MobileDomainSettingsScreen.tsx` now uses `normalizeDnsRecords()` with `verificationRecords`, `configuredBy`, and fallback CNAME handling.
- The combined screen now derives DNS rows from `domainStatus.config || domainStatus.verification` so add-domain and refresh responses use the same display path.
- `scripts/verification/verify-menulist-api-tenant-safety.js` now guards the active mobile Domain Settings screen for normalized DNS rows and rejects raw domain-status config rendering.

Validation:

```bash
npm run verify:menulist-api-tenant-safety
npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false --pretty false
git diff --check
```

Cost/deploy boundary: this is MenuList mobile UI display hardening only. It adds no Firestore reads/writes/deletes, Storage operations, provider calls, cache invalidations, rules, indexes, schema changes, Cloud Function logic changes, owner-facing settings, Firebase deploy requirement, or Vercel deploy action in this session. Existing custom-domain add/check/remove behavior, subdomain save/check behavior, Vercel calls, store writes, and public cache invalidation are unchanged.

## June 29 Follow-up: Mobile Domain Remove Failure Guard

The mobile custom-domain mutation sweep found that desktop custom-domain removal used `axios.delete('/api/domain')`, which rejects non-2xx responses before local UI state changes, but the active mobile Domain Settings remove path used `fetch('/api/domain', { method: 'DELETE' })` without checking `response.ok`. A failed route or provider-side delete could therefore clear `customDomain` and `domainVerified` from local state and show saved, even though the server still owned the domain.
